title: 第1章 刘济民
content_zh:
1978年3月2号，刚过完春节，距离春天的故事还差一年，准确的说是542天。

    黄沙遮天蔽日，再次笼罩了整座燕京城，天地一片暗黄。可对于此时的中国人来说，无疑是兴奋的。

    从高空俯瞰，一团黑点正在缓慢地往前移动，这个黑点正是刘济民。

    大街小巷里，人们连呼吸都变得极为困难，更别提行走了。不知道谁家的铁皮桶被大风吹倒了，在大街上叮叮当当四处乱滚。

    漫天风沙中，刘济民歪歪扭扭地骑着自行车，他上半身弓成了虾背，双脚用力猛蹬，两只手死死握住车把以维持巧妙的平衡。

    因为太过用力，脸憋得通红，咬着牙，像是五十岁便秘的大爷，要用尽全身的力气把最后一截给顶出来。

    这辆73年的破永久自行车上装了一副棉质挡风袖筒，但不仅不挡风，风还从车把缝里直往里钻，他的双手冻得近乎失去了知觉。

    “砰——咚——吱扭”，当车发出“咣当”一声，刘济民就知道快到家了。

    小巷子坑坑洼洼，刘济民冻僵的双手被震得发麻。因为风沙大，他要使劲儿眯着眼睛防止风沙进了眼，这让他的视线更加受限了。如刀的寒风中夹杂着沙粒，打的他脸生疼。

    阳光透过黄色的阴云，使整个世界都变成了一片暗黄色。地面和墙壁上都覆盖着一层薄薄的黄沙，斑驳的矮墙上，早已枯萎的杂草随风摇摆。

    刘济民骑着自行车叮叮当当地穿过小巷，碾过坑坑洼洼的路面，穿过三四个胡同口，终于到菊儿胡同了。

    刘济民翻身跳下自行车，接着抱起自行车朝菊儿胡同3号院内走去。大院的门槛被踩出来了一个缺口，红漆大门早已褪色，发白的对联只剩下了一角，狭窄的夹道里摆着各种各样的杂物。

    刘济民望着眼前破旧古早的一切，一切那么真实，又觉得那么模糊，像是走进了年代剧里，黄沙则是天然的怀旧滤镜。

    菊儿胡同3号院，本是老佛爷绯闻男友、青梅竹马荣禄的四合院。除此之外，菊儿胡同的5号，以及寿比胡同的6号院，都是荣禄的宅子。

    3号院本来是跟大院一进连着，如今中间砌了墙，想要到3号院，只能走旁边的夹道。屁大点地方住了三十多口人，有普通市民，还有一些是单位的房子。

    要是瓜尔佳氏看到这一幕，估计气得要进宫面圣。

    夹道里堆着杂物，刘济民抱着自行车不时被东西绊到。他将没公德心的邻居骂了一遍，不过只能在心里骂，嘴里嘟囔一句，没准就被隔壁的大爷大妈听去了。

    在这种地方生活，放个屁都能砸到别人的脚面上，干啥事儿都得悠着点儿。当然，绝大多数时候，大爷大妈都称得上热心。

    夹道内行数十步，廓然开朗。院子里电线杂乱无章，纵横交错，各种用具都具有浓厚的年代色彩，颜色单调，就连飞奔上墙的猫都是灰黑色的。

    有的几户关系好，大家共建了一个厨房，一起用。有的则是在门口砌了一个灶台，或者用煤炉做饭。

    现在是上班时间，又或者天太冷，大家躲在屋子里不愿意出来。

    刘济民像是闯进院子里的不速之客，他更是闯进这个时代的不速之客。

    刘济民重生了，当他醒来的时候，正坐在中国医学科学院的教室，听老师讲述如何将“防病治病和阶级斗争相结合”。

    刘济民原本是某顶流211中文系的研究生，硕士毕业后在河南文联下面的《奔流》杂志工作。

    可惜热爱文学的他，赶上了纯文学末法时代。整个杂志社的知名度，不如网文一句“恐怖如斯”高。

    跟纯文学拥趸一样，他也不服网文的影响力，在编辑任上，决定大力挖掘出几篇“名作”。可惜现实还是给他上了一课，最后只能将自己的“雄心壮志”揉吧揉吧塞嘴里咽了。
content_en:
March 2, 1978, just after the Spring Festival, there is still one year left before the story of spring, 542 days to be precise.

    The yellow sand covered the sky and the sun, once again covering the entire Yanjing City, making the sky and the earth a dark yellow. But for the Chinese people at this time, it is undoubtedly exciting.

    Looking down from a high altitude, a group of black dots was slowly moving forward. This black dot was none other than Liu Jimin.

    In the streets and alleys, it has become extremely difficult for people to even breathe, let alone walk. Someone's tin bucket was blown over by the strong wind, and was clanging and rolling around on the street.

    In the wind and sand, Liu Jimin was riding a bicycle crookedly. His upper body was arched like a shrimp's back, his feet were pedaling hard, and his hands were tightly holding the handlebars to maintain a delicate balance.

    Because he had exerted too much force, his face was red from holding it in, and he was gritting his teeth, like a fifty-year-old man with constipation, trying to use all his strength to push out the last part.

    This 1973 old bicycle was equipped with a pair of cotton windshield sleeves, but not only did they not block the wind, the wind also penetrated through the cracks in the handlebars. His hands were so cold that he almost lost consciousness.

    "Bang - bang - squeak", when the car made a "bang" sound, Liu Jimin knew he was almost home.

    The alley was full of potholes, and Liu Jimin's frozen hands were numb from the shock. Because of the strong wind and sand, he had to squint hard to prevent the sand from entering his eyes, which further restricted his vision. The cold wind like a knife was mixed with sand, which hurt his face.

    The sun shines through the yellow clouds, turning the whole world into a dark yellow. The ground and walls were covered with a thin layer of yellow sand, and on the mottled low walls, long-withered weeds swayed in the wind.

    Liu Jimin rode his bicycle jingling through the alleys, over the bumpy roads, and passed through three or four alley entrances before finally arriving at Ju'er Hutong.

    Liu Jimin turned over and jumped off his bicycle, then picked up the bicycle and walked towards No. 3 Ju'er Hutong. There was a gap in the courtyard's threshold. The red paint on the gate had long faded. Only a corner of the white couplets remained. There were all kinds of sundries in the narrow passage.

    Liu Jimin looked at the dilapidated and ancient things in front of him. Everything was so real and yet felt so blurry, as if he had stepped into a period drama, and the yellow sand was a natural nostalgic filter.

    Courtyard No. 3 in Ju'er Hutong was originally the courtyard home of Lafayette's rumored boyfriend and childhood sweetheart Ronglu. In addition, No. 5 in Ju'er Hutong and No. 6 in Shoubi Hutong are both Ronglu's houses.

    Courtyard No. 3 was originally connected to the main courtyard, but now there is a wall in the middle. If you want to get to Courtyard No. 3, you can only take the side road. There are more than 30 people living in this big place, including ordinary citizens and some units.

    If Guarjia saw this scene, he would probably be so angry that he would go to the palace to face the saint.

    There were piles of debris in the aisle, and Liu Jimin tripped over things from time to time while holding his bicycle. He scolded his unethical neighbor, but he could only scold him in his heart and mutter something, which might be heard by the uncle and aunt next door.

    Living in a place like this, your farts can hit other people's feet, so you have to take your time in everything you do. Of course, most of the time, uncles and aunts can be called enthusiastic.

    After walking dozens of steps along the road, it becomes clear and cheerful. The electric wires in the yard are messy and criss-crossed, and all kinds of appliances have a strong sense of the times and are monotonous in color. Even the cat flying up the wall is gray and black.

    Some households have such good relations that they all build a kitchen and use it together. Some built a stove at the door or used a coal stove to cook.

    It's working time now, or maybe it's too cold and everyone is hiding in the house and doesn't want to come out.

    Liu Jimin is like an uninvited guest breaking into the courtyard, and he is even more like an uninvited guest breaking into this era.

    Liu Jimin was reborn. When he woke up, he was sitting in a classroom at the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, listening to the teacher talk about how to "combine disease prevention and treatment with class struggle."

    Liu Jimin was originally a graduate student in the top 211 Chinese Department. After graduating with a master's degree, he worked at the "Benliu" magazine under the Henan Federation of Literary and Art Circles.

    It is a pity that he, who loves literature, caught up with the era of pure literature and the end of the Dharma. The popularity of the entire magazine is not as high as the sentence "It's so scary" in an online article.

    Like fans of pure literature, he was also dissatisfied with the influence of online articles. During his tenure as editor, he decided to dig out a few "masterpieces." Unfortunately, reality still taught him a lesson, and in the end he could only rub and stuff his "ambition" into his mouth and swallow it.
